title: Cover and Extraction
premise: Freya Okafor, a hostage negotiator whose one public failure still haunts the service, works deniable cases for an intelligence unit that prefers its successes unattributed. When their former handler Marcus Vane—officially dead for two years—sends them a calendar invitation for a meeting tomorrow, Freya is pulled into a conspiracy inside their own agency: a staged 'accident' designed to kill a whistleblower and bury evidence of a compromised extraction Freya once survived. Torn between loyalty to the institution that made them and the truth about the night that broke them, Freya races to stop the attack while unraveling who killed Vane—and discovers the invitation itself was his final negotiation. In the end, Freya chooses truth over duty, exposes the operation at devastating personal cost, and finally faces the failure on the board, learning it was never theirs to carry.
about_author: Odile Dunmore is a former crisis-line counselor turned novelist who writes thrillers about people forced to choose between the institutions they serve and the truths they can't unknow. She lives in coastal Maine, where she claims the fog helps her plot.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Working a thankless bank-siege negotiation, Freya gets a calendar ping: 'Vane, 0800 tomorrow.' Marcus Vane has been dead two years. Freya talks the gunman down flawlessly—unattributed, as always—but can't shake the message. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in routine; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Flashback-tinged introduction to Freya's role in the shadow unit and the Kestrel House failure that made their name a liability. Their supervisor, Halloran, warns them off 'ghost mail.' Freya checks the meeting coordinates anyway. Emotional beat: loneliness of invisible competence.

chapters.title: Dead Man Dialing
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The meeting spot is empty except for a burner phone playing a voicemail Vane recorded before he died: he found something in the files of Operation Nightjar—the extraction Freya survived—and someone killed him for it. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Nightjar
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya digs into Nightjar and finds the official record contradicts their own memory: three hostages listed as rescued were never recovered. One name matches the failure on the board. Emotional beat: memory as unreliable ground; vertigo.

chapters.title: Halloran's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Halloran. Inside the agency, Halloran learns Freya received Vane's message and quietly flags them for surveillance, torn between protecting Freya and protecting the operation. Emotional beat: institutional love curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't Rescued
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya tracks Ilse Brandt, a Nightjar hostage officially dead but alive under a new identity. Ilse confirms the extraction was sabotaged from inside to silence her testimony about arms shipments. Emotional beat: the board's failure reframed—someone else wrote it.

chapters.title: Old Partners
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya turns to Tomas Reyes, their former partner and the only person who knew them during Nightjar. Tomas is warm, helpful—and lying about small things. Emotional beat: intimacy shadowed by suspicion; love against duty begins here.

chapters.title: Accident, Scheduled
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Decoding Vane's voicemail metadata, Freya finds a date, a venue, and a contractor's invoice: a gas-system 'maintenance' job at a government archive building—an attack dressed as infrastructure failure, set for eleven days out. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Surveillance State of Mind
chapters.summary: POV Halloran. Halloran confronts Freya with fabricated evidence that Vane was a traitor, offering redemption if Freya stands down. Freya recognizes the negotiation technique—being used on them. Emotional beat: the negotiator negotiates for their own soul.

chapters.title: What Vane Taught Me
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Interleaved flashbacks to Vane mentoring Freya: 'Every hostage wants one thing—to be believed.' Freya realizes Vane planned this trail deliberately, each clue a proof point a skeptic would need. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into method.

chapters.title: Ilse's Price
chapters.summary: POV Ilse Brandt. Ilse agrees to testify but demands Freya first admit publicly what really happened at Nightjar—including Freya's own split-second choice that saved some lives and doomed others. Emotional beat: accountability as the price of alliance.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya spots their own surveillance team and runs a counter-game through the city, realizing only three people could have ordered the tail. One of them is Tomas. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: POV Freya. In Vane's storage unit, Freya finds a recording: the saboteur's voice, partially redacted, plus a second invitation—'If you're hearing this, they've moved the date up.' The attack is now six days away. Emotional beat: the floor drops out.

chapters.title: Loyalty Audit
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Tomas, complicit but not murderous, wrestles with covering for Halloran's operation because exposing it would destroy the unit—and Freya with it. He deletes one file and keeps another. Emotional beat: duty as a slow moral surrender.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya and Ilse map the archive building's gas systems and identify the exact maintenance window. They need the work order signed off internally—which means walking back into the agency and asking Halloran directly. Emotional beat: audacity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Negotiating with Your Boss
chapters.summary: POV Freya. In a masterful cat-and-mouse scene, Freya baits Halloran into revealing knowledge of the revised date—a detail only the plotters would know. Halloran realizes the trap too late. Emotional beat: checkmate disguised as small talk.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Halloran. Exposed, Halloran accelerates the timeline to forty-eight hours and orders Freya's termination as a rogue asset. Tomas is ordered to do it. Emotional beat: the machine choosing efficiency over people.

chapters.title: The Rooftop
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Tomas corners Freya on a rooftop; instead of killing them, he hands over the last authentication key and confesses his role, asking Freya to remember who he was before duty hollowed him. Sirens below. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved in sacrifice.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: POV Freya. With Tomas's key and Ilse's testimony, Freya triggers the building's own safety interlocks and alerts emergency services anonymously, forcing an evacuation that makes the 'accident' impossible to stage cleanly. Emotional beat: turning the enemy's cover story into their exposure.

chapters.title: Detonation Deferred
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The attack fails; the premature gas release injures no one but leaves forensic fingerprints leading straight to Halloran's contractors. Halloran attempts to flee and is arrested mid-extraction—in a mirror of Nightjar. Emotional beat: grim symmetry; justice without triumph.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: POV Freya. At the inquiry, Freya testifies to everything, including their own choice at Nightjar, accepting censure to clear the dead hostages' names. The failure comes off the board—not erased, but correctly attributed. Emotional beat: truth as costly, necessary homecoming.

chapters.title: Cover Story
chapters.summary: POV Freya, months later. Officially reassigned, unofficially free, Freya visits Vane's grave and leaves a phone playing a single word: 'Believed.' A new case file waits—but this time Freya chooses it in daylight. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; visibility as victory.
